subject: maths
title: Grid References and Maps: Compass Points, Directions and Pathways
seo_title: Year 4 Grid References and Maps Worksheets: 8 Compass Points and Directions (Free)
standard_text: Create and interpret grid reference systems using grid references and directions to locate and describe positions and pathways
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths worksheets on grid references and maps: read and write grid references like B3, use the 8 compass points, follow directions and describe pathways on grid maps. 100 questions with an answer key, aligned to the Australian Curriculum.
key_big: A grid reference gives the letter (across) first, then the number: B3.
key_sub: Give directions as a compass point and a number of squares. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on. North-east is halfway between north and east.
body_html:
Grid references

A grid map has letters across the top and numbers down the side. A grid reference such as E3 names one square. Go across to the letter first, then down to the number.

Example

What is the grid reference of the bakery?

Go across to column F, then down to row 1. Write the letter first.

Answer: F1

Some maps number the rows from the bottom up. Always check where row 1 is.

The eight compass points

North is usually at the top of a map. The four main points, going clockwise, are north, east, south and west (“Never Eat Soggy Weet-Bix”). Halfway between them are north-east, south-east, south-west and north-west. North or south always comes first: NE, not EN.

On the mapDirection
upnorth (N)
up and rightnorth-east (NE)
righteast (E)
down and rightsouth-east (SE)
downsouth (S)
down and leftsouth-west (SW)
leftwest (W)
up and leftnorth-west (NW)

A quarter turn moves 2 points round the compass. A half turn takes you to the opposite direction.

Follow and give directions

Give the direction and the number of squares (or steps). Count the squares you move, not the square you start on. One square north-east means one square up and one square right, across the corner.

Example

On the park map, describe the dashed path from the rotunda to the sandpit.

The rotunda is in C5. Go 1 square north to C4, then 2 squares east to E4.

Answer: 1 north, 2 east

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing the number first (3B)Letter first, across; then the number: B3
Mixing up east and westEast is on the right of the map, west on the left
Naming in-between points the wrong way (east-north)North or south comes first: north-east
Turning the wrong wayClockwise goes the same way as the hands of a clock: N, NE, E, SE and so on
Counting the starting squareCount the moves, not the square you stand on

faq.q: What do Year 4 students learn about grid references in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: In Year 4 (AC9M4SP02) students create and read grid reference systems. They use grid references like B3 and directions such as north-east with a number of squares to find places and describe pathways.

faq.q: How do you read a grid reference like B3?
faq.a: Go across to column B first, then down (or up) to row 3. The letter always comes first.
North, north-east, east, south-east, south, south-west, west and north-west, going clockwise. The in-between points always start with north or south.
No. NAPLAN is for Years 3, 5, 7 and 9. Map and grid reference skills from Year 4 help students prepare for the Year 5 NAPLAN numeracy test.

sets.title: Read and write grid references like B3

items.q: What is the grid reference of the café?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The café is in column E, row 3: E3. Always write the letter first, so not 3E.

items.q: What is in square E5?
items.e: Go across to column E first, then down to row 5. Square E5 is the vet.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the cinema?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The cinema is in column C, row 5: C5. Always write the letter first, so not 5C.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the pool?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The pool is in column A, row 2: A2. Always write the letter first, so not 2A.

items.q: Which place covers squares A5 and B5?
items.e: Row 5 is the bottom row. Squares A5 and B5 are the first two squares in it: the train station.

items.q: What is in square E2?
items.e: Go across to column E first, then down to row 2. Square E2 is the chemist. Reading the number as the column (column B, row 5) gives the train station.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the bakery?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The bakery is in column F, row 1: F1. Always write the letter first, so not 1F.

items.q: What is in square C1?
items.e: Go across to column C first, then down to row 1. Square C1 is the library. Reading the number as the column (column A, row 3) gives the fire station.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the post office?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The post office is in column E, row 1: E1. Always write the letter first, so not 1E.

items.q: What is in square F3?
items.e: Go across to column F first, then down to row 3. Square F3 is the bus stop.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the bank?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The bank is in column F, row 2: F2. Always write the letter first, so not 2F.

items.q: Which place is in the same row as the pool?
items.e: The pool is in A2, so it is in row 2. The chemist is in E2, also row 2. The fire station is in A3: same column, not the same row.

items.q: The school covers more than one square. Which squares?
items.e: The school covers 2 squares: A1 and B1. Letter first, then number, for each square.

items.q: The park covers more than one square. Which squares?
items.e: The park covers 4 squares: B2, C2, B3 and C3. Letter first, then number, for each square.

items.q: What is in square B4?
items.e: Go across to column B first, then down to row 4. Square B4 is the police station.

items.q: What is in square A3?
items.e: Go across to column A first, then down to row 3. Square A3 is the fire station. Reading the number as the column (column C, row 1) gives the library.

items.q: What is in square D4?
items.e: Go across to column D first, then down to row 4. Square D4 is the supermarket.

items.q: Which square is empty?
items.e: D2 is in column D, row 2. Nothing is drawn there. C2 is part of the park, E2 is the chemist and D4 is part of the supermarket.

items.q: Kai says the police station is in 4B. What should he write?
items.e: Kai has the number first. A grid reference gives the letter first (across), then the number (down): B4.

items.q: The hospital covers more than one square. Which squares?
items.e: The hospital covers 2 squares: F4 and F5. Letter first, then number, for each square.

sets.title: The eight compass points: N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW

items.q: Ethan faces south. He makes a quarter turn anticlockwise. Which way does he face now?
items.e: Use the compass rose. A quarter turn moves you 2 points, from one main direction to the next. From south, move two compass points anticlockwise: east. Turning the other way would give west.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight north-east from the entrance?
items.e: North-east is up and to the right on the map. From the entrance (C5), move one square at a time diagonally: the first place is the platypus in D4. Going north-west by mistake gives the toilets.

items.q: Liam faces north. He makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now?
items.e: Use the compass rose. A quarter turn moves you 2 points, from one main direction to the next. From north, move two compass points clockwise: east. Turning the other way would give west.

items.q: The café is ___ of the aviary.
items.e: The aviary is in E1 and the café is in F1. From the aviary, go 1 square right (east). So the café is east of the aviary.

items.q: The kangaroos are ___ of the dingoes.
items.e: The dingoes are in C3 and the kangaroos are in D2. From the dingoes, go 1 square right (east) and 1 square up (north). The same number each way is a diagonal, so the kangaroos are north-east of the dingoes. Check east (right) and west (left) carefully: north-west would be the other way.

items.q: The reptiles are ___ of the dingoes.
items.e: The dingoes are in C3 and the reptiles are in A3. From the dingoes, go 2 squares left (west). So the reptiles are west of the dingoes.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight north-west from the dingoes?
items.e: North-west is up and to the left on the map. From the dingoes (C3), move one square at a time diagonally: the first place is the wombats in B2. Going north-east by mistake gives the kangaroos.

items.q: The platypus is ___ of the kangaroos.
items.e: The kangaroos are in D2 and the platypus is in D4. From the kangaroos, go 2 squares down (south). So the platypus is south of the kangaroos.

items.q: Sienna faces east. She makes a half turn. Which way does she face now?
items.e: Use the compass rose. A quarter turn moves you 2 points, from one main direction to the next. From east, move four compass points (to the opposite side): west.

items.q: What is the opposite direction to north-east?
items.e: Opposite means a half turn. Turn north-east halfway round the compass: south-west. Both parts change: north to south and east to west.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight south-west from the aviary?
items.e: South-west is down and to the left on the map. From the aviary (E1), move one square at a time diagonally: the first place is the kangaroos in D2.

items.q: Amelia faces north-east. She makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does she face now?
items.e: Use the compass rose. A quarter turn moves you 2 points, from one main direction to the next. From north-east, move two compass points clockwise: south-east. Turning the other way would give north-west.

items.q: What is the short way to write north-west?
items.e: Use the first letter of each word, in order: North-West is NW. North or south always comes first.

items.q: The reptiles are ___ of the emus.
items.e: The emus are in C1 and the reptiles are in A3. From the emus, go 2 squares left (west) and 2 squares down (south). The same number each way is a diagonal, so the reptiles are south-west of the emus. Check east (right) and west (left) carefully: south-east would be the other way.

items.q: William faces north-west. He makes a three-quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now?
items.e: Use the compass rose. A quarter turn moves you 2 points, from one main direction to the next. From north-west, move six compass points clockwise (the same as a quarter turn anticlockwise): south-west. Turning the other way would give north-east.

items.q: The play area is ___ of the seals.
items.e: The seals are in E3 and the play area is in F4. From the seals, go 1 square right (east) and 1 square down (south). The same number each way is a diagonal, so the play area is south-east of the seals. Check east (right) and west (left) carefully: south-west would be the other way.

items.q: The toilets are ___ of the entrance.
items.e: The entrance is in C5 and the toilets are in B4. From the entrance, go 1 square left (west) and 1 square up (north). The same number each way is a diagonal, so the toilets are north-west of the entrance. Check east (right) and west (left) carefully: north-east would be the other way.

items.q: Going clockwise: N, NE, E, ___, S. Which compass point is missing?
items.e: After east (E), going clockwise towards south (S), the next point is south-east (SE). Write S first: SE, not ES.

items.q: Which direction is halfway between south and west?
items.e: The in-between directions always start with north or south: south-west (SW), not west-south. South-east is between south and east.

items.q: The koalas are ___ of the reptiles.
items.e: The reptiles are in A3 and the koalas are in A1. From the reptiles, go 2 squares up (north). So the koalas are north of the reptiles.

sets.title: Follow directions on a grid map

items.q: Start at the kiosk. Go 2 squares south, then 2 squares west. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at F1. Go 2 squares south to F3, then 2 squares west to D3. The pond is in D3. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at the gum tree.

items.q: Grace starts at the red dot in A1. She goes 3 squares south-east. Which square does she finish in?
items.e: Start at A1. Go 3 squares south-east to D4. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at C3.

items.q: Ruby starts at the red dot in E5. She goes 2 squares north-west, then 1 square north. Which square does she finish in?
items.e: Start at E5. Go 2 squares north-west to C3, then 1 square north to C2. Swapping the two numbers of squares gives D2.

items.q: Start at the rotunda. Go 1 square north-east, then 1 square east. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at C5. Go 1 square north-east to D4, then 1 square east to E4. The sandpit is in E4. Mixing up east and west gives the toilets.

items.q: Start at the skate park. Go 1 square north-east, then 2 squares north. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at A5. Go 1 square north-east to B4, then 2 squares north to B2. The BBQ is in B2.

items.q: Start at the tap. Go 2 squares south-west, then 1 square south. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at F2. Go 2 squares south-west to D4, then 1 square south to D5. The bench is in D5.

items.q: Start at the gate. Go 1 square south-east, then 3 squares east. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at A1. Go 1 square south-east to B2, then 3 squares east to E2. The gum tree is in E2. Swapping the two numbers of squares gives the sandpit.

items.q: On a grid map, letters go across (A, B, C and so on) and numbers go down (1, 2, 3 and so on). A toy robot starts at F6 and moves 2 squares west, then 3 squares north. Where is it now?
items.e: Moving east or west changes the letter. Moving north or south changes the number (south adds, north takes away). 2 squares west changes the letter from F to D; 3 squares north changes the number from 6 to 3. The answer is D3.

items.q: Harper starts at the red dot in F2. She goes 4 squares west. Which square does she finish in?
items.e: Start at F2. Go 4 squares west to B2. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at C2.

items.q: Start at the car park. Go 4 squares north, then 2 squares west. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at F5. Go 4 squares north to F1, then 2 squares west to D1. The swings are in D1. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at the gum tree.

items.q: Ava starts at the red dot in A3. She goes 3 squares east, then 2 squares north. Which square does she finish in?
items.e: Start at A3. Go 3 squares east to D3, then 2 squares north to D1. Mixing up north and south gives D5.

items.q: On a grid map, letters go across (A, B, C and so on) and numbers go down (1, 2, 3 and so on). A toy robot starts at D5 and moves 1 square east, then 4 squares north. Where is it now?
items.e: Moving east or west changes the letter. Moving north or south changes the number (south adds, north takes away). 1 square east changes the letter from D to E; 4 squares north changes the number from 5 to 1. The answer is E1.

items.q: On a grid map, letters go across (A, B, C and so on) and numbers go down (1, 2, 3 and so on). A toy robot starts at B2 and moves 3 squares east, then 2 squares south. Where is it now?
items.e: Moving east or west changes the letter. Moving north or south changes the number (south adds, north takes away). 3 squares east changes the letter from B to E; 2 squares south changes the number from 2 to 4. The answer is E4.

items.q: Charlotte starts at the red dot in B4. She goes 3 squares east. Which square does she finish in?
items.e: Start at B4. Go 3 squares east to E4. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at D4.

items.q: On a grid map, letters go across (A, B, C and so on) and numbers go down (1, 2, 3 and so on). A toy robot starts at G7 and moves 2 squares north-west. Where is it now?
items.e: Moving east or west changes the letter. Moving north or south changes the number (south adds, north takes away). 2 squares north-west changes the letter from G to E and the number from 7 to 5. The answer is E5. A diagonal move changes both the letter and the number.

items.q: On a grid map, letters go across (A, B, C and so on) and numbers go down (1, 2, 3 and so on). A toy robot starts at C1 and moves 3 squares south-east. Where is it now?
items.e: Moving east or west changes the letter. Moving north or south changes the number (south adds, north takes away). 3 squares south-east changes the letter from C to F and the number from 1 to 4. The answer is F4. A diagonal move changes both the letter and the number.

items.q: Start at the toilets. Go 2 squares north-east, then 1 square north. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at A4. Go 2 squares north-east to C2, then 1 square north to C1. The slide is in C1.

items.q: Cooper starts at the red dot in B5. He goes 2 squares north-east, then 2 squares east. Which square does he finish in?
items.e: Start at B5. Go 2 squares north-east to D3, then 2 squares east to F3. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at D4.

items.q: Mia starts at the red dot in F1. She goes 2 squares south-west, then 2 squares south. Which square does she finish in?
items.e: Start at F1. Go 2 squares south-west to D3, then 2 squares south to D5. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at E3.

items.q: Chloe starts at the red dot in E5. She goes 3 squares north. Which square does she finish in?
items.e: Start at E5. Go 3 squares north to E2. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at E3.

items.q: How many squares long is the dashed path from the gate to the rotunda?
items.e: Add the squares of each part: 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 6 squares. Count the moves, not the gate square you start on.

items.q: Noah walks from the car park: 2 north, 1 west, 1 north. He reaches the gum tree. Which directions take him back the same way?
items.e: To go back the same way, do the moves in reverse order and turn each direction to its opposite: 1 south, 1 east, 2 south.

items.q: Which directions describe the dashed path from the car park to the gum tree?
items.e: Start at F5. Go 2 squares north to F3, then 1 square west to E3, then 1 square north to E2. That is the gum tree.

items.q: Which one straight line takes you from the toilets to the swings?
items.e: The toilets are in A4 and the swings are in D1. That is 3 squares east and 3 squares north: the same number each way, so it is a diagonal. Go 3 squares north-east.

items.q: Aarav walks from the bench to the BBQ. He moves only north, south, east or west, and only through empty squares. What is the fewest number of squares he can move?
items.e: The bench is in D5 and the BBQ is in B2: 2 squares across and 3 squares up or down. 2 + 3 = 5 squares, and there is a way round through empty squares that is this short. Do not count the starting square.

items.q: Which directions describe the dashed path from the BBQ to the swings?
items.e: Start at B2. Go 2 squares east to D2, then 1 square north to D1. That is the swings.

items.q: Which directions take you from the gate to the sandpit?
items.e: The gate is in A1 and the sandpit is in E4. A to E is 4 squares east. Row 1 to row 4 is 3 squares south. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on.

items.q: Which directions take you from the swings to the bench without walking through the pond?
items.e: Start at D1. Go 1 square east to E1, then 4 squares south to E5, then 1 square west to D5. That is the bench, and the path never enters the pond (C3 and D3). “4 south” walks through the pond. “1 west, 4 south, 1 east” walks through the pond.

items.q: Which directions take you from the slide to the toilets?
items.e: The slide is in C1 and the toilets are in A4. C to A is 2 squares west. Row 1 to row 4 is 3 squares south. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on.

items.q: Which directions describe the dashed path from the gate to the rotunda?
items.e: Start at A1. Go 2 squares south to A3, then 1 square east to B3, then 2 squares south to B5, then 1 square east to C5. That is the rotunda.

items.q: Which directions take you from the rotunda to the kiosk?
items.e: The rotunda is in C5 and the kiosk is in F1. C to F is 3 squares east. Row 5 to row 1 is 4 squares north. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on.

items.q: Which directions describe the dashed path from the skate park to the bench?
items.e: Start at A5. Go 1 square east to B5, then 1 square north to B4, then 2 squares east to D4, then 1 square south to D5. That is the bench.

items.q: Which one straight line takes you from the tap to the rotunda?
items.e: The tap is in F2 and the rotunda is in C5. That is 3 squares west and 3 squares south: the same number each way, so it is a diagonal. Go 3 squares south-west.

items.q: Which directions take you from the car park to the BBQ?
items.e: The car park is in F5 and the BBQ is in B2. F to B is 4 squares west. Row 5 to row 2 is 3 squares north. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on.

items.q: Which directions take you from the tap to the skate park?
items.e: The tap is in F2 and the skate park is in A5. F to A is 5 squares west. Row 2 to row 5 is 3 squares south. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on.

items.q: Which directions take you from the BBQ to the sandpit without walking through the pond?
items.e: Start at B2. Go 2 squares south to B4, then 3 squares east to E4. That is the sandpit, and the path never enters the pond (C3 and D3). “1 south, 3 east, 1 south” walks through the pond.

items.q: Jack walks from the rotunda: 1 north, 2 east. He reaches the sandpit. Which directions take him back the same way?
items.e: To go back the same way, do the moves in reverse order and turn each direction to its opposite: 2 west, 1 south.

items.q: Which one straight line takes you from the car park to the sandpit?
items.e: The car park is in F5 and the sandpit is in E4. That is 1 square west and 1 square north: the same number each way, so it is a diagonal. Go 1 square north-west.

items.q: Isla walks from the gate to the rotunda. She moves only north, south, east or west, and only through empty squares. What is the fewest number of squares she can move?
items.e: The gate is in A1 and the rotunda is in C5: 2 squares across and 4 squares up or down. 2 + 4 = 6 squares, and there is a way round through empty squares that is this short. Do not count the starting square.

items.q: Which directions describe the dashed path from the rotunda to the sandpit?
items.e: Start at C5. Go 1 square north to C4, then 2 squares east to E4. That is the sandpit.

sets.title: Real-life map problems: camps, streets and bushwalks

items.q: Year 4 is on school camp. Each square is 50 metres. Jack walks from the archery 4 squares east, then 2 squares north to the flying fox. How far does he walk?
items.e: He walks 4 + 2 = 6 squares. 6 × 50 = 300 metres. Only counting the east part gives 4 × 50 = 200 metres.

items.q: On a bushwalk map, Ethan walks 3 squares north-east, then 3 squares south-east. Where is he now, compared with the start?
items.e: North-east goes up 3 and right 3. South-east goes down 3 and right 3. The ups and downs cancel out, and he went 3 + 3 = 6 squares right: east.

items.q: Kai’s tent is at C4 on the campsite map. The toilets are 3 squares east of his tent. What is the grid reference of the toilets?
items.e: East is across, so the letter changes and the number stays the same. C, then D (1), E (2), F (3): F4. Counting C as 1 gives E4.

items.q: On the oval, Sienna walks 2 squares north, then 2 squares east. Which one direction takes her straight back to where she started?
items.e: Sienna went north and east, so to come back she goes the opposite way: south and west. 2 each way is a diagonal: south-west.

items.q: Year 4 is on school camp. Which squares does the lake cover?
items.e: The lake is in columns D and E, rows 3 and 4: D3, E3, D4 and E4.

items.q: Year 4 is on school camp. What is in square B4?
items.e: Column B, row 4 is the archery. Reading the number as the column (column D, row 2) gives the dining hall.

items.q: Year 4 is on school camp. The archery is ___ of the campfire.
items.e: The campfire is in A3 and the archery is in B4: 1 square right (east) and 1 square down (south). That is south-east.

items.q: Year 4 is on school camp. What is 1 square south-west of the flying fox?
items.e: South-west is down and to the left. From F2, one square down and one square left is E3, part of the lake.

items.q: On a street map, the letters go across and the numbers go down. The beach is in B2 and the surf club is in B5. Which direction is the surf club from the beach?
items.e: Both are in column B, so the direction is straight up or down. The number goes from 2 to 5, which is down the map: south.

items.q: Year 4 is on school camp. What is the grid reference of the flying fox?
items.e: Go across to column F, then down to row 2: F2. Letter first, then number.

items.q: Year 4 is on school camp. Zara is at the toilets, facing north. She makes a quarter turn clockwise, then walks 3 squares. What does she reach?
items.e: Facing north, a quarter turn clockwise makes her face east. 3 squares east of A5 is D5: the canoes.

items.q: On a map of a farm, the dam is in C2 and the shed is in F2. How many squares east is it from the dam to the shed?
items.e: Count the moves from C: D (1), E (2), F (3). That is 3 squares east. Counting C as well gives 4.

items.q: Year 4 is on school camp. Which directions take you from the toilets to the office?
items.e: The toilets are in A5 and the office is in D1. A to D is 3 squares east. Row 5 to row 1 is 4 squares north.

items.q: Liam writes the grid reference of the canteen on a school map as 3E. What should he write?
items.e: Write the letter first and then the number. 3E has them the wrong way round; E3 is right. C5 swaps the letter and number positions.

items.q: Year 4 is on school camp. Each square on the map is 50 metres. How far is it from the campfire straight south to the toilets?
items.e: From A3 to A5 is 2 squares. 2 × 50 = 100 metres. Counting the campfire square too gives 3 squares, or 150 metres.

items.q: Year 4 is on school camp. What is the first place you reach going straight north-east from the archery?
items.e: North-east is up and to the right. From B4: C3 is empty, then D2 is the dining hall. North-west would give the campfire.

items.q: A treasure hunt clue says: “Start at A1. Go 4 squares east, then 3 squares south.” Letters go across and numbers go down. Where is the treasure?
items.e: 4 squares east changes A to E. 3 squares south changes 1 to 4. The treasure is in E4. Counting the starting square gives D3.

items.q: Year 4 is on school camp. From the campfire, the class walks 1 square north-east, then 1 square east. Where are they?
items.e: Start at A3. Go 1 square north-east to B2, then 1 square east to C2. C2 is part of the dining hall.

items.q: Each square on a map of the town is 100 metres. The pool is 4 squares west of the school, in the same row. How far is the pool from the school?
items.e: 4 squares × 100 metres = 400 metres. Counting the school square as well gives 5 squares, or 500 metres.

items.q: On a bushwalk map, the lookout is 3 squares north-west of the car park. Which direction is the car park from the lookout?
items.e: To go back, turn to the opposite direction. The opposite of north-west is south-east.
